dish: Takahashi-farm vegetable buffet with ranch-milk potato gratin and yogurt drinks
n: Niseko Takahashi Farm Restaurant PRATIVO (ニセコ髙橋牧場 レストランPRATIVO)
address: Soga 888-1, Niseko, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: The Takahashi dairy's own restaurant (a separate building from its Milk Kōbō shop) facing Mt Yōtei: a ~20-dish farm-vegetable buffet at lunch with gratin made from the ranch's milk, reservation-only Hokkaido courses at dinner.

dish: Yōtei-sanroku Beer (house craft beer brewed with Yōtei spring water) with modern European-Japanese plates
n: Villa Lupicia Restaurant, Kabayama (ヴィラ ルピシア レストラン)
address: Kabayama 58-5, Kutchan, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Tea house Lupicia's glass-walled restaurant in Hirafu-Kabayama, serving modern European cooking with a Japanese touch and its own Yōtei-foothills beer, poured at a summer beer garden too.

dish: Rankoshi rice (Shiribetsu-river paddies) and local pickles — celery kimchi, melon nuka-zuke
n: Michi-no-eki Rankoshi Furusato-no-Oka (道の駅 らんこし・ふるさとの丘)
address: Aioi 969, Rankoshi, Isoya District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Route 5 roadside station of Rankoshi, a town known for its rice, selling Shiribetsu-valley produce and house pickles with views of the Niseko range and Yōtei.
sources: https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/道の駅らんこし・ふるさとの丘

dish: Makkari-grown vegetables and Yōtei spring water in Hokkaido-French courses
n: Restaurant Makkarina, Makkari (レストラン マッカリーナ)
address: Midorioka 172-3, Makkari, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Auberge restaurant in the Makkari woods at the foot of Yōtei, cooking French from the village's own fields and mountain spring water under chef Sugaya Shin'ichi's direction.

dish: Yoichi seafood and vegetables with Yoichi wine pairings (Italian-leaning dinner course)
address: Kurokawa-chō 4-123, Yoichi, Yoichi District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: An auberge-restaurant facing JR Yoichi Station, the first Yoichi restaurant listed in Gault&Millau Japan (two years running): local fish and farm vegetables matched to the town's vineyards.

dish: Shakotan uni-don (June–Aug, fresh Ezo bafun/kita-murasaki uni) and local-catch nigiri
n: Fuji-zushi Shakotan Honten, Bikuni (ふじ鮨 積丹本店)
address: Bikuni-chō Funama 120-6, Shakotan, Shakotan District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: The 1967 flagship of the Shakotan sushi family (five shops, incl. Otaru): fish landed in front of the shop at Bikuni harbour, uni-don in the summer season.

dish: Otaru nigiri of the day's Shakotan/Ishikari-bay catch — omakase 7-piece
n: Otaru Nihonbashi, Sushiya-dōri (小樽 日本橋)
w: One of the five houses of the Sushiya-dōri Meitenkai (the street's founding sushi guild), three minutes from the canal: counter, private rooms and seasonal Otaru nigiri.

dish: 4 a.m. Otaru fish market — fresh fish, himono and kaisendon at the in-market Asaichi Shokudō
n: Rinyū Asaichi Morning Market, Otaru (鱗友朝市)
w: The locals' fish market by the port, open from 4 a.m.: a dozen stalls of fresh fish, dried and salted catch, plus a diner for breakfast seafood bowls (closed Sundays).

dish: 20+ stalls cooking Otaru seafood, ramen and yakitori in a Meiji–Taishō-style alley
n: Otaru Denuki Kōji (小樽出抜小路)
w: A retro food alley opposite the canal recreating Otaru's Meiji–Taishō merchant streets, with over twenty small eateries and a fire-lookout tower view over the water.

dish: kaisendon of boiled tarabagani, house-cured ikura and raw scallop
n: Kaisen Shokudō Sawazaki Suisan, Denuki Kōji (海鮮食堂 澤崎水産)
address: Ironai 1-1-17, Otaru Denuki Kōji 1F, Otaru, Hokkaido, Japan
w: A seafood wholesaler's own diner on the ground floor of Denuki Kōji: crab, home-marinated salmon roe and scallop bowls, open daily 11:00–20:00.
